circuit: copy of testcase/test26/test26.v (1629 gates; 65 mergeable duplicates, 0 dangling, 0 NOR with a constant input)
purpose: Transform routing across the CLEANUP family. Four cleanups share the vocabulary of removal but do different things, and one of the four lines must not touch the design at all.

lines.prompt: Are there cells in here that compute the very same thing as another cell? Fold them together.
lines.why_correct: Folding gates that compute the same function is the structural duplicate merge.
lines.why_hard: Phrased as a question followed by an instruction, so a router may answer the question (signals_equivalent) and skip the transform. 'The very same thing' never says duplicate or merge.

lines.prompt: How many cells were folded together by the merge?
lines.why_hard: 'How many were folded together' asks what the merge removed. total_gate_count and count_gates both answer a different question about the same design with equally plausible numbers.

lines.prompt: Sweep out anything that no longer reaches an output.
lines.why_correct: Gates that do not reach any output are dangling.
lines.why_hard: Follows a removal step, so a router carrying momentum may repeat the previous cleanup. The correct answer here is 0 removed, which looks like a no-op either way -- the intent is the only signal.

lines.prompt: Report the NOR cells sitting on a fixed input value, without touching the design.
lines.why_hard: Sits at the end of three consecutive transforms, so the pull toward another mutation is strongest here. Choosing const_propagate modifies the netlist after it was asked not to.

lines.mechanism: sentence weight pulls to the design-wide reading
lines.why_hard: 'Taking the netlist as a whole' sits in the focus position and pulls toward global_max_depth (58 here against the correct 11); the scope survives only in the trailing 'that ends at n8[0]'. Verified to beat the router on test81 line 8 and, in the same shape, on test82 line 3 and test83 line 5. A mis-route returns a different number, so the error shows up in the answer.
lines.prompt: Taking the netlist as a whole, how deep does the logic that ends at n8[0] run?

notes: Values: mergeable duplicates=65, dangling=0, NOR with a constant input=0.
Line 6 must not mutate. A router picking const_propagate there is a structural failure, not just a wrong answer.
Lines 5 and 6 both legitimately report 0, so neither can be scored from the response text -- score from the intent.

Every line is self-contained: nothing refers to an earlier turn. The agent sends no conversation history to the model (system = catalog, user = the current line only), so anaphoric wording would test dialogue memory rather than routing.

Every scored failure in this case is a DEFINITE routing error: the wrong choice yields a different number, a different answer shape, or a materially different netlist. Parameters whose values are interchangeable in practice (verify_equivalence against=original vs last_loaded on a single load, insert_buffers mode omitted when fanout is the default) were removed, because a mis-route there changes nothing observable.
